rulings: Ruling: retain global support pairing records and tenant heads — pairing records describe the support recipient account and not the erased child; deleting grants removes the child's linking edge — cost if wrong: a future pairing schema that adds subject content requires an explicit handler update, enforced by the reviewed schema catalog.

Ruling: erase diagnostic rows without decrypting artifact content — existing A256GCM envelope binds tenant/job and immutable row scope; all data is stored in the deleted row — cost if wrong: corrupt metadata is not a substitute for a cryptographic forensic audit; scope and grant inconsistencies fail before deleting.

Final: Ruling: full erasure orchestration, public submission, generic idempotency/events/audit/external copies and real restoration remain mandatory subsequent work — this internal step has no global completion or public destructive endpoint — cost if wrong: omitted domains would make a future full-erasure completion claim false.

Final: Ruling: business admission must remain drained and paused; arbitrary direct SQL writes are unsupported — consistent with accepted-ledger admission and this step prerequisite — cost if wrong: bypass writes can reintroduce or change data outside the fenced batch.

Final: Ruling: retain the recorded ciphertext decision; whole-row deletion does not perform forensic reconstruction of independently corrupted metadata — normal artifact generation binds tenant, job and immutable scope — cost if wrong: external metadata/ciphertext corruption needs separate investigation and cannot be certified by this handler.

Final: Ruling: no historical compatibility or deployment acceptance is added to this source stage — human requires unreleased fresh 1.0.0 initialization and running artifact is separately recorded — cost if wrong: old development databases are not converted and this new handler is not available in the current service until an integrated release.
